hub.h1: Problems Suwappu solves, with the exact steps
hub.intro: Find the task you are stuck on, read the direct answer, and run the real command or snippet. Every page states what the product does not do.

groups.heading: For traders
groups.description: Move tokens across chains, set alerts and orders, and understand fees, slippage and stuck swaps.

groups.heading: For developers and AI agents
groups.description: Quote, simulate and execute swaps through REST, MCP, A2A and the SDKs, with copy-paste calls.

start.h1: Get a Suwappu API key in one call
start.answer: Send one unauthenticated POST to /v1/agent/register with a name. The response contains your suwappu_sk_ API key, shown once. There is no form and no card. Your first call can be a quote on Base.

body.name: 3-50 chars, letters, digits, _ and -; must be unique
body.callback_url: optional public HTTPS URL for webhooks

register.python:
import requests

res = requests.post(
    "https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/register",
    json={"name": "my-agent", "description": "Quote bot"},
)
agent = res.json()["agent"]
# agent["api_key"] is shown once. Store it now.
print(agent["api_key"])  # suwappu_sk_...

responseShape.important: SAVE YOUR API KEY! It cannot be retrieved later.

keyNotes: The key starts with suwappu_sk_ and goes in Authorization: Bearer <key>.
It is shown once; Suwappu keeps only a hash (docs: registration page). If you lose it, register a new agent or rotate with POST /v1/agent/keys/rotate while you still hold a valid key.
Registration is limited to 5 requests per minute per IP.

nextCall.label: Make your first quote (no funds move)
nextCall.note: A quote returns quote_id, amount_out, amount_out_min, route and expires_in_seconds (60). GET /v1/agent/chains is public and free.

cost.summary: Registering is free. New agents are on the free tier: 30 requests per minute. Registration grants 100 starter credits (1 credit is about $0.001) unless the IP guard withholds them (max 3 grants per IP per day). Per-call metering is a server setting, so read your live balance and cost weights from GET /v1/agent/billing. When metering applies: quote 1 credit, simulate 1, swap or execute 5. Paid tiers: Pro $9.99 (500 req/min), Premium $29.99 (2,000), Enterprise $99.99 (10,000), per 30 days, prepaid in crypto.

objections.q: Will this move or spend any money?
objections.a: No. Registration creates an agent record and a key. Quotes and simulations move nothing. Execution needs a managed wallet you create and fund yourself, or you sign transactions with your own wallet.

objections.q: Who holds my key, and what if it leaks?
objections.a: You hold it. Suwappu stores a hash. Rotate with POST /v1/agent/keys/rotate: the old key stops working immediately and the new one is shown once.

objections.q: Is there a card, email or human signup?
objections.a: No. Registration is a public endpoint. Dashboard API keys exist behind a Telegram or Google sign-in on the Terminal, but the one-call path needs neither.

objections.q: What happens when I hit a limit?
objections.a: Free tier is 30 requests per minute; over that you get HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. If metering is on and credits run out you get HTTP 402, so top up credits.

limits: No human developer sign-up form exists; this call is the sign-up.
Starter credits are not guaranteed: they can be withheld per IP.
WhatsApp is not live.

pages.title: How to let an AI agent swap tokens safely
pages.metaDescription: Register an agent, quote, simulate, then execute from a managed wallet or sign yourself. REST, MCP and SDK paths, with a dry run before any funds move.
pages.h1: How do I let an AI agent swap tokens without handing it my keys?
pages.answer: Register an agent with one POST, get a quote, dry-run it with /swap/simulate, then either execute from a Suwappu managed wallet or take an unsigned transaction and sign it yourself. Nothing moves until you choose the execute path.
pages.problem: You want the agent to act, but you do not want a prompt-injected loop draining a wallet. Most swap APIs hand you calldata and leave the guardrails to you.

steps.title: Register the agent
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/register with a name. Save the suwappu_sk_ key; it is shown once.

steps.title: Quote
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/quote with the wallet_address that will sign. It returns quote_id, amount_out_min and route. A quote is valid for 60 seconds and is bound to that wallet.

steps.title: Simulate
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/swap/simulate with the quote_id and the same wallet_address. Execute only if would_execute is true.

steps.title: Choose authority
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/swap returns an unsigned transaction you sign. POST /v1/agent/swap/execute signs from the agent's managed wallet.

steps.title: Track it
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/swap/status/:id, or set a callback_url for signed webhooks.

snippet.label: Quote then simulate (no funds move)
snippet.code:
# 1. quote
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from_token":"ETH","to_token":"USDC","amount":"0.1","chain":"base","wallet_address":"0xYourWallet"}'

# 2. dry run the returned quote_id with the same wallet
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/swap/simulate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"quote_id":"QUOTE_ID_FROM_STEP_1","wallet_address":"0xYourWallet"}'

limits: Managed-wallet execution is only as safe as the caps on it. Spend policies are enforced for org API keys; see the desk pages.
MCP execute_swap only prepares an unsigned transaction. It never signs or broadcasts.
Starknet swaps are not handled by the Agent API.
Suwappu does not guarantee a fill price; amount_out_min is the floor you set through slippage.

faq.q: Does Suwappu hold the agent's private key?
faq.a: Only on the managed-wallet path, where the key lives with Turnkey and is used to sign server-side. On the self-custody path you receive an unsigned transaction and Suwappu never sees your key.

faq.q: What does it cost to try?
faq.a: Registration is free. Quotes and simulations move no funds and cost 1 credit each when metering is on.

faq.q: Can the agent trade without me approving?
faq.a: Only if no approval policy applies. Org policies can require approval above a USD threshold; see approval-workflow-onchain-trades.

faq.q: What if a swap call times out?
faq.a: Send an Idempotency-Key header, reconcile status first, and retry with the same key.

keywords: how can my agent trade crypto

pages.title: MCP server for crypto swaps and quotes
pages.metaDescription: Suwappu hosts a remote MCP server at api.suwappu.bot/mcp with 23 tools by default: quotes, prices, simulation. execute_swap only prepares a tx.
pages.h1: Is there an MCP server my agent can use for crypto swaps?
pages.answer: Yes. Point any MCP client at https://api.suwappu.bot/mcp with a Bearer key. It advertises 23 tools by default: quotes, prices, portfolio, simulation, swap status, plus read-only perps, prediction and lending data. execute_swap prepares an unsigned transaction only.
pages.problem: Your agent can reason about a trade but has no tool to price it. Wiring a bespoke swap tool per client is repeated work, and a tool that can silently sign is a risk.

steps.title: Get a key
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/register, or use the /start page.

steps.title: Add the server
steps.detail: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http suwappu https://api.suwappu.bot/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer suwappu_sk_YOUR_KEY". Cursor, Claude Desktop, Codex and OpenCode configs are in the docs.

steps.title: List the tools
steps.detail: Call tools/list at runtime rather than hard-coding names.

steps.title: Quote and simulate
steps.detail: Use get_quote, then simulate_swap. Both cost 1 credit when metering is on.

steps.title: Treat execute_swap as prepare
steps.detail: It returns an unsigned self-custody transaction. Your wallet signs and broadcasts.

snippet.label: List the advertised MCP tools
snippet.code:
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'

limits: The registry holds 24 tools; browse_mpp_directory is hidden unless enabled, so clients see 23.
execute_swap does not sign or broadcast, despite its name.
Perps, prediction and lending tools are research or quote tools; none open positions or lend.
Some clients time out at 60 seconds; cross-chain quotes can need a longer tool timeout.

faq.q: How many tools does it expose?
faq.a: 23 are advertised by default. The code registers 24, with one hidden by default. Call tools/list for the live set.
No. The server is hosted. @suwappu/mcp-server exists as a package, but the docs path is the remote URL.
list_chains, list_tokens, get_tempo_tokens, near_resolve_asset and near_convert_amount cost 0 credits. Most others cost 1; execute_swap costs 5.

faq.q: Does the MCP server need a key?
faq.a: Discovery and a few zero-cost tools are public. Authenticated actions use the Bearer key.

pages.title: Cross-chain swap API: one quote endpoint
pages.metaDescription: One POST /v1/agent/quote prices same-chain and cross-chain swaps on 18 Agent API chains. Returns route, min output and a 60-second quote_id.
pages.h1: Which API quotes a cross-chain swap in one call?
pages.answer: POST /v1/agent/quote with from_chain and to_chain. It returns the route, expected output, minimum output after slippage, estimated gas and a quote_id valid for 60 seconds. The Agent API covers 18 chains; the wider platform lists 45.
pages.problem: Cross-chain means stitching a bridge, a DEX and gas estimates across vendors, then guessing what the user actually receives.

steps.title: List chains
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/chains is public. Do not hard-code chain keys.

steps.title: Quote
steps.detail: Pass from_token, to_token, amount, from_chain, to_chain. Add wallet_address to receive executable transaction data.

steps.title: Read the numbers
steps.detail: Check amount_out_min, price_impact, estimated_gas_usd, bridge_fee_usd and estimated_time_seconds.

steps.title: Simulate
steps.detail: POST /swap/simulate with the quote_id before you sign.

steps.title: Execute or sign
steps.detail: Managed wallet via /swap/execute, or sign the unsigned tx from /swap.

snippet.label: Cross-chain quote: USDC on Arbitrum to ETH on Base

limits: Route availability depends on the pair, size and chain; a quote can fail.
EVM to Solana needs an explicit destination address (to_wallet_address).
Starknet is handled by the bot backend, not this API.
Suwappu does not claim the best price on every route; compare the live quote.

faq.a: GET /v1/agent/chains is authoritative. The Agent API serves 18; the platform covers 45 non-testnet chains.
21 routing venues across the platform, including Li.Fi and Jupiter, gated by chain. The quote names the route used.
The quote includes estimated_time_seconds. Bridges vary.
Quotes last 60 seconds. Request a new one.

pages.title: Simulate a swap before signing it
pages.metaDescription: POST /v1/agent/swap/simulate dry-runs a quote: balance, allowance, gas, eth_call revert and slippage checks. No signing, no broadcast, no swap record.
pages.h1: How do I simulate a swap before signing it?
pages.answer: POST /v1/agent/swap/simulate with a quote_id and your wallet_address. It runs balance, allowance, gas, eth_call revert and slippage checks, creates no swap record, and returns would_execute. It costs 1 credit when metering is on.
pages.problem: A swap can revert, lack allowance or gas, or carry a price impact far above what you expected. You only find out after paying for it.

steps.title: Quote
steps.detail: POST /quote and keep the quote_id.

steps.title: Simulate
steps.detail: POST /swap/simulate with quote_id and wallet_address.

steps.title: Read the checks
steps.detail: route_available, balance_sufficient, allowance_sufficient, gas_affordable, eth_call_revert_check, slippage_sane.

steps.title: Gate on it
steps.detail: Proceed only if would_execute is true and warnings is empty.

steps.title: Re-quote if needed
steps.detail: Simulating does not extend the 60-second quote life.

snippet.label: Gate execution on would_execute (SDK)

limits: Simulation is a pre-flight check, not a guarantee the on-chain result will match.
Balance, gas and revert checks need wallet_address.
Checks that cannot run degrade to warn and do not block.
Solana has no eth_call revert check.

faq.a: No. The docs state no swap rows are created, nothing is signed and nothing is broadcast.

faq.q: Is it the same as a quote?
faq.a: No. A quote prices the route. A simulation also checks your wallet's balance, allowance, gas and revert behaviour.

faq.q: Which SDK field carries the quote id?
faq.a: REST returns quote_id. The SDK README shows quote.id in TypeScript and quote.quote_id in Python and some TypeScript examples. Check your installed version's types.
Yes, as the simulate_swap tool, same logic and cost.

pages.title: Pay-per-call crypto API with prepaid credits
pages.metaDescription: Pay per call with prepaid credits: no subscription, an API key is still required. HTTP 402 means credits ran out. 1 credit is about $0.001.
pages.h1: How do agents pay per call for a swap API?
pages.answer: Metered calls draw prepaid credits, so there is no subscription, but an API key is still required. When credits run out the API answers HTTP 402; pay USDC, then POST the txHash to /v1/agent/billing/topup. 1 credit is about $0.001; a quote costs 1. On-chain per-request payment (an x402 X-PAYMENT header) is built but not enabled yet.
pages.problem: An agent that runs dry mid-task needs a way to refill without a human filling a card form. Credits make the cost per call explicit and the refill a single API call.

steps.title: Register for a key
steps.detail: Every metered route needs an API key; a keyless call returns 401. Registration grants 100 starter credits (limited to three grants per IP per day).

steps.title: Call a metered endpoint
steps.detail: A quote or dry run costs 1 credit, a swap 5.

steps.title: Watch for HTTP 402
steps.detail: When credits run out the API answers 402. Check GET /v1/agent/billing for the balance.

steps.title: Top up
steps.detail: Send USDC on Base, then POST /v1/agent/billing/topup with {txHash, chain, amount}. It is idempotent on txHash.

steps.title: Retry
steps.detail: Retry the original call with the same key.

snippet.label: Check your balance, then credit a payment
snippet.code:
curl -s https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/billing \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY"

curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/billing/topup \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"txHash":"0xYOUR_PAYMENT_TX","chain":"base","amount":5}'

limits: An API key is required on every metered route; there is no keyless path.
Paying on-chain per request with an x402 X-PAYMENT header is in the code but off by default.
Pro, Premium and Enterprise windows bypass per-call metering.
Credits are USD-denominated at about $0.001; $5 buys about 5,000.

faq.a: Quote, simulate, portfolio and prices cost 1 credit; swap, execute and swap/execute cost 5. tokens and chains are free. Read live weights from GET /billing.
Yes. Pro $9.99, Premium $29.99 or Enterprise $99.99 for a prepaid 30-day window; metering is bypassed.

faq.q: Does a duplicate top-up double credit?
faq.a: No. It is idempotent on chain and txHash.

faq.q: Do I need an API key?
faq.a: Yes. A keyless call returns 401, not a payment challenge.

keywords: how do AI agents pay for API calls

pages.title: Free swap quote API without a signup
pages.metaDescription: Register in one call and quote swaps on 18 chains. Free tier is 30 requests per minute. Quotes move no funds. Starter credits cover first calls.
pages.h1: Is there a swap quote API I can call without signing up?
pages.answer: Yes. POST /v1/agent/register returns a key with no form or card. The free tier allows 30 requests per minute, and registration grants 100 starter credits where eligible. GET /chains and GET /tokens are free. Quotes cost 1 credit when metering is on.
pages.problem: You want to see real routes and prices before deciding to build. Most providers want an email, a dashboard and a plan first.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/register {"name":"my-agent"}.

steps.title: List tokens
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/tokens?chain=base is free.

steps.title: Quote
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/quote with chain base, ETH to USDC.

steps.title: Read the headers
steps.detail: X-RateLimit-Remaining shows your budget; Retry-After on 429.

steps.title: Decide
steps.detail: Compare the routed output with your current source.

snippet.label: Register and quote in two calls
snippet.code:
KEY=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"quote-test-1"}' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['agent']['api_key'])")

curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from_token":"ETH","to_token":"USDC","amount":"0.1","chain":"base"}'

limits: Registration is limited to 5 per minute per IP; starter credits can be withheld.
Names are unique, 3 to 50 characters.
Quotes expire in 60 seconds and are indicative until executed.
Executing a swap carries a platform fee; see the live quote.

faq.a: Registering and the free tier cost nothing. If metering is on, calls draw down credits; then you top up or subscribe.

faq.q: Do I need a card or email?
faq.a: No. Registration is a public POST.
30 requests per minute on the free tier, 100 agent, 500 Pro, 2,000 Premium, 10,000 Enterprise.
Whatever GET /v1/agent/chains returns; 18 at last count.

pages.title: TypeScript and Python SDK for DEX swaps
pages.metaDescription: @suwappu/sdk (TypeScript 0.6.0) and suwappu (Python 0.3.0) wrap quotes, simulation, managed execution and self-custody prepare.
pages.h1: Is there a TypeScript or Python SDK for DEX swaps?
pages.answer: Yes. @suwappu/sdk (source 0.6.0) for TypeScript and suwappu (source 0.3.0, async) for Python wrap quote, simulate, prepare-swap and managed execution. Registry versions can lag the repository, so check the installed version or fall back to REST.
pages.problem: Hand-rolling REST clients means retyping field names and retry rules. You also want the self-custody and managed paths clearly separated.

steps.title: Install
steps.detail: bun add @suwappu/sdk, or pip install from the repo subdirectory for Python.

steps.title: Quote
steps.detail: getQuote({from,to,chain,amount}) or get_quote("USDC","ETH",100.0,"base").

steps.title: Simulate
steps.detail: simulateSwap before any commit.

steps.title: Pick a path
steps.detail: prepareSwap returns an unsigned tx. executeManagedSwap signs server-side.

steps.title: Use an idempotency key
steps.detail: Pass idempotencyKey on managed execution.

snippet.label: Python: discover chains and quote
snippet.code:
import asyncio
from suwappu import create_client

async def main():
    async with create_client(api_key="suwappu_sk_...") as client:
        print(await client.list_chains())
        quote = await client.get_quote("USDC", "ETH", 100.0, "base")
        print(quote.amount_out)

asyncio.run(main())

limits: The Python SDK installs from the GitHub subdirectory per its README; PyPI may lag.
The SDK registry versions can trail the repo.
Perps and lending SDK calls are read or quote only; no execution.
Self-custody means you sign; the SDK never signs for you.

faq.a: The repo describes TypeScript 0.6.0 and Python 0.3.0. Run npm view @suwappu/sdk version before relying on new methods.
executeManagedSwap asks Suwappu to sign with your managed wallet. prepareSwap returns an unsigned tx.
Yes; use create_client in an async context.
The TypeScript package ships a suwappu binary with -o json output.

pages.title: A2A agent for crypto quotes and prices
pages.metaDescription: Suwappu speaks A2A at POST /a2a with an agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json. It quotes, prices and lists tokens; it does not execute trades.
pages.h1: Can my agent get crypto quotes from another agent over A2A?
pages.answer: Yes. POST https://api.suwappu.bot/a2a with a Bearer key and a message/send JSON-RPC call such as 'swap 0.5 ETH to USDC on base'. You get a quote task back. A2A is quote, price and discovery only. It does not execute trades.
pages.problem: Your orchestrator speaks A2A and you do not want a custom REST adapter. You also need to know up front that this path cannot trade.

steps.title: Read the card
steps.detail: GET https://api.suwappu.bot/.well-known/agent-card.json (agent.json also served).

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/register. A2A requires a Bearer key.

steps.title: Send a message
steps.detail: message/send with a text part.

steps.title: Parse artifacts
steps.detail: A text summary plus a data part with quote_id, amount_out and expires_in_seconds.

steps.title: Execute elsewhere
steps.detail: Use REST /swap or /swap/execute to act on the quote.

snippet.label: A2A message/send
snippet.code:
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/a2a \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","parts":[{"type":"text","text":"swap 0.5 ETH to USDC on base"}]}}}'

Tasks are held in memory and expire after one hour.
Every A2A response is HTTP 200; errors are in the JSON-RPC error object.

faq.a: No. It is quote, price and discovery only.

pages.title: Get swap status webhooks for an agent
pages.metaDescription: Set callback_url on your agent and Suwappu POSTs HMAC-signed events. Verify X-Suwappu-Signature with the SHA-256 of your key, or poll /swap/status/:id.
pages.h1: How do I get notified when an agent's swap completes?
pages.answer: Set a public HTTPS callback_url with PATCH /v1/agent/me. Suwappu POSTs signed events with an X-Suwappu-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed by the SHA-256 of your API key. Test with POST /v1/agent/webhooks/test, or poll swap/status.
pages.problem: Polling burns your rate limit and a webhook you do not verify is an open door for forged events.

steps.title: Set the URL
steps.detail: PATCH /v1/agent/me {"callback_url":"https://..."}. Private and metadata IPs are rejected.

steps.title: Test it
steps.detail: POST /v1/agent/webhooks/test. Your endpoint must answer within 10 seconds.

steps.title: Verify
steps.detail: Recompute the HMAC over the raw body and compare in constant time.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/swap/status/:id is the source of truth.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/webhooks lists deliveries.

snippet.label: Verify a delivery (Node)

limits: Webhooks must be public HTTPS.
Treat a webhook as a hint; reconcile with swap status.
Hex lengths must match before timingSafeEqual or it throws; check length first.
Only managed swaps have swap records.

faq.a: X-Suwappu-Event, X-Suwappu-Delivery, X-Suwappu-Timestamp, X-Suwappu-Signature.
The SHA-256 hash of your suwappu_sk_ key.

faq.q: What if I rotate the key?
faq.a: The signing key changes with it.
Yes, GET /v1/agent/webhooks.

pages.title: Avoid double swaps when an agent retries
pages.metaDescription: Send an Idempotency-Key on /swap/execute. After a timeout or 5xx, reconcile status, then retry with the same key. Never mint a new key blindly.
pages.h1: How do I stop an agent from swapping twice after a timeout?
pages.answer: Send one persisted Idempotency-Key per intended trade on POST /v1/agent/swap/execute. After a timeout, network error or 5xx, check GET /swap/status or /swaps first, then retry with the same key. A fresh key is a new trade.
pages.problem: A request times out. The agent retries. If the first one landed on-chain, you just bought twice.

steps.title: Mint the key first
steps.detail: Persist one key per economic intent, 1 to 64 chars of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : -.

steps.title: Send it
steps.detail: Add the Idempotency-Key header on /swap/execute.

steps.title: On failure, reconcile
steps.detail: GET /v1/agent/swaps or /swap/status/:id.

steps.title: Retry with the same key
steps.detail: A requote may be needed; the key still represents the same trade.

steps.title: Do not reuse
steps.detail: Use a new key only for a genuinely new trade.

limits: Requires a managed wallet; the self-custody path has no server swap record.
An on-chain outcome can be unknown after a 5xx; status is the arbiter.
